       Glenn Hodge, Ryan Hodge, Schwertner Farms, Inc., JT Carothers
Holdings, LLC, and MCP18 LLC (together, the Hodge-Schwertner Intervenors)
timely ﬁle this Initial Post-Hearing Brief under SOAH Order No. 6 and the orders
entered during the hearing on the merits.

                               Statement of the Case
         Under the Public Utility Regulatory Act (PURA), an electric utility must
obtain a certiﬁcate of convenience and necessity (CCN) from the Public Utility
Commission of Texas (PUC or Commission) to install, operate, or extend electric
utility service to the public. 1 To approve an application to obtain or amend a CCN,
the PUC must ﬁnd the proposed CCN is “necessary for the service,




       1
           Tex. Util. Code Ann. (PURA) § 37.051.

                    Hodge-Schwertner Intervenors; Initial Post-Hearing Brief

 accommodation, convenience, or safety of the public.” 2 Texas statutes 3 and PUC
rules 4 govern Commission approval of CCN applications. They set forth
the criteria according to which the PUC is to make its determination and include
several factors that the Commission must consider when choosing a route for a
transmission line.
          Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Service
Corporation (together, Applicants) ﬁled a joint application to amend their CCNs
for the Bell County East Switch to Big Hill Substation 765-kV Transmission Line
Project in Bell, Burnet, Concho, Coryell, Lampasas, Llano, Mason, McCulloch,
Menard, Milam, Mills, San Saba, Schleicher, Tom Green, and Williamson
Counties, Texas. 5
          The Hodge-Schwertner Intervenors participate in this docket because
proposed links and routes aﬀect their properties, families, community, and long-
term land-use interests. The Hodge interests and JT Carothers Holdings/MCP18
concerns are tied most directly to the Salado-area E-link impacts and prudent-
avoidance concerns, including Link E12; they support Route 894 █ . Schwertner
Farms has separate land-planning and agricultural/business concerns, including
Links E2, E4, E51, and F01, but supports Route 894 and does not support Route
392 █ . 6
          Applicants selected Route 894 █ as the route that best addresses the
Commission’s routing criteria. Route 894 is also recommended by Brian C.
Andrews, who independently evaluated the Application, the Environmental
Assessment and Routing Study, the routing and GIS data, the RFI responses,
and the relevant hearing record. 7

                              Summary of the Argument
        Route 894 █ best satisﬁes the balancing required by PURA § 37.056(c)(4)
and 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B). That conclusion rests on two converging route-
selection analyses. Applicants identiﬁed Route 894 as the route that best addresses
the Commission’s routing criteria after holistically analyzing the 122 ﬁled routes.12
Mr. Andrews independently reached the same conclusion after reviewing the
Application, the Environmental Assessment, route data, RFIs, GIS data, and the
hearing record. 13
        The route-selection question turns on two links. Among all the links in the
study area, E6 and E12 are the habitable-structure outliers, carrying dozens of
homes where the typical link has about one. Route 894 █ avoids both while
balancing cost and habitable-structure impacts: no less-expensive ﬁled route has
fewer habitable structures, and the only ﬁled routes that do cost far more. 14 That
is why Route 894 is more than a route that avoids a speciﬁc set of concerns, it is
the best balance.

because it is the best overall route, but the Commission need not accept E12

        Route 894 █ combines superior performance on Mr. Andrews’ relative

14.001, 32.001, 37.051, 37.053, 37.054, and 37.056. SOAH has jurisdiction to

            1. Link E12 is an outlier, not an ordinary link.

        Link E6 has 77 habitable structures, the highest link in the study area.
Link E12 has 40, the second highest. The median link has one habitable structure,
the mean is 4.1, and 77% of links have ﬁve or fewer. Only E6 and E12 reach 40. 22
        That outlier status is a function of methodology applied uniformly, not
of selective counting. On cross-examination, Applicants’ witness panel conﬁrmed
that the habitable-structure counts are tabulated using the same 500-foot
centerline buﬀer methodology across all 171 alternative links and every ﬁled route,
without variation by link, route, or party.23 The same protocol that yields E6’s 77
structures and E12’s 40 yields the one-structure median across the remaining
links. E12’s count therefore reﬂects exposure measured by a uniform protocol,
not an analytical artifact or a single-ﬁlter selection. 24

recommending Route 487 █ . On cross-examination, he agreed that E12 is in the
same general Salado-area part of the map, that E12 has 40 habitable structures,

             2. Route-Level Comparison

         Section 37.056 of PURA sets out factors the Commission must consider
in deciding whether to grant a CCN application. 27 The Commission’s rule adds
additional factors governing the routing of transmission lines.28 While no route
is better than all the other routes in all respects, Route 894 █ best meets the
criteria of PURA and the Commission’s rules.29
         These statutory and rule factors are stated in broad terms and necessarily
compete, so the Commission’s task is not to optimize any single metric but to
accommodate the competing routing interests and select the route with the best
overall balance. 30 Route 894 █ is that route. It leads or ties the routes of interest
on habitable structures, on park foreground visual zone, and on avoidance of the
E6 and E12 outliers, while remaining within the reasonable range of the ﬁled-route
data on cost, length, and paralleling. No competing route improves on any one
factor without giving back more on the others, which is why Route 894 is the best
composite outcome even though it is not the single least-expensive route.
